title: Recursive merge walks __proto__ and pollutes Object.prototype
root_cause: mergeConfig recursively assigns attacker-controlled keys including __proto__, so a JSON payload can set properties on Object.prototype.
attacker_model: Anyone who can supply the patch object — typically untrusted JSON from a network client or config file — after JSON.parse (which preserves a literal __proto__ key).
attack_path: mergeConfig({}, parsed) walks keys and recurses into __proto__
impact: Integrity break: attacker-controlled properties appear on unrelated objects; can escalate to auth bypass or option injection depending on how properties are read.
guarantee_broken: Object prototype integrity / safe merge of untrusted objects
how_to_disprove: After mergeConfig({}, JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"polluted":"yes"}}')), a fresh {} must not have polluted === 'yes'.
summary: Recursive merge of attacker-supplied JSON walks __proto__, allowing prototype pollution.
